scope: Terminal interpolation immediately rounded toF32 only. This is our derivation under explicit assumptions, not an externally reviewed theorem or model qualification.
assumptions: IEEE round-to-nearest-even FP32/FP64 with gradual underflow; no contraction except explicitF32FMA. No overflow in TwoSum or other operations.
Eight finiteF32donors with M=max(abs(donor)) in[2^-60,2^60]. Other ranges use originalF64fallback. Fractions are the same clampedF64fractions as reference and lie in[0,1].
Normalized pairs represent exact sum hi+lo, with hi=RN32(hi+lo) and lo the exact residual. General TwoSum is used, not magnitude-conditional FastTwoSum.

Every fast result with either rounded endpoint equal to zero falls back, avoiding reliance on real-valued enclosures to establish signed-zero bits. Nonfinite inputs and uncertain rounding also fall back.
rounding_model: For an M-scaledF32 operation, abs(rounding error)<=u*abs(exact result)+alpha*M, where u=2^-24,alpha=u^2. This includes subnormal rounding because eta32/2<=alpha*M throughout the guard. Unit-scaled fraction operations use M=1.
derivation: Fraction splitting: h=RN32(f), l=RN32(f-double(h)); the F64subtraction is exact by Sterbenz when h!=0 (within a factor of2), and trivial when h=0. Total represented fraction error is at most3alpha; TwoSum renormalization preserves its represented value.
For any normalized M-scaled operand with represented abs value<=8M, use abs(hi)<=16M and abs(lo)<=16uM. Unit-factor represented abs<=2 gives abs(hi)<=4 and abs(lo)<=4u.

Pair add: TwoSum of high components is exact; separately round the sum of low components and its addition to the high residual, then normalize by TwoSum. The two low-order rounding errors total less than256alpha*M.

Pair multiply: p=RN32(ahi*bhi), e=FMA32(ahi,bhi,-p), c1=RN32(ahi*blo), c2=RN32(alo*bhi), c=RN32(c1+c2), z=RN32(e+c), then TwoSum(p,z). Account for rounding of the FMA residual and all cross terms, plus the omitted alo*blo. Error is less than1024alpha*M; no error-free product assumption is needed.

A lerp computes pairdiff=b-a, pairproduct=pairdiff*fhat, pairadd=a+pairproduct. Diff error is amplified by at most2; multiplication/addition and fraction truncation contribute another1024+256+12 units ofalpha*M. Total local error<=1804alpha*M.

Seven nested x/y/z lerps have three dependency levels. Exact interpolation at each level is convex, so prior absolute error is not amplified. Total error<=5412alpha*M. This also proves finalized pair values remain below2M, while differences/products remain below8M; the operand bounds are maintained inductively.

ReferenceF64rounding: each complemented fraction differs from its exact real complement by at most2u64. Three factor errors plus three product roundings bound each weight error by12u64. Donor multiplication adds2u64*M, so each term error<=14u64*M. Eight ordered additions each add at most33u64*M with unrounded partial sums below32M. Total<=376u64*M<512u64*M, including F64subnormal absolute errors.
Reconstructing the normalized pair as RN64(double(hi)+double(lo)) adds at mostalpha*M. Combining paired error, ordered-reference error and reconstruction gives5429alpha*M, below65536alpha*M=2^-32*M.

Radius B=double(M)*2^-32 is exact normalF64. RD64(A-B) and RU64(A+B) enclose the original un-clippedF64reference. If clipping is requested, applying the identical monotone clamp to both endpoints preserves inclusion.
If the two enclosure endpoints round to the same nonzeroF32bitpattern, monotonic RN conversion proves the originalF64reference rounds to that pattern. Otherwise execute the originalF64calculation.
